title: LiteratureTree
description: A novelty tree: a variable-depth concept classification. Two isomorphic tree types share this one structure and renderer, distinguished by node kind: a technical tree is topic → task → pipeline → module(optional) → 论文(叶); a challenge tree is topic → challenge → insight → 论文(叶). Internal nodes are abstract concepts; papers are leaves referenced by resource_id. A flat paper_list is the single metadata ledger — the tree references its entries by id. One doc = one tree; the two tree types live in separate docs sharing the same paper_list (INV25 一文多树).

paper_list.description: Flat 全集 ledger of every collected paper. Single source of paper metadata; tree nodes reference these by resource_id. A paper may be listed with classified=false (collected but not yet placed in the tree).

importance.description: One of founding / milestone / representative; the renderer appends a star badge (★★★/★★/★).

doi.description: Retained as a dedup identity field; NOT rendered as a table column.

asset_note.description: vault-relative path of this paper's assets note (paper_assets/<year>-<first-author>-<title>.md), authored by the skill. The paper list links to it in the Assets column.

concept.description: An internal tree node = an abstract concept. The root is kind=topic. A technical tree descends topic → task → pipeline → module(optional); a challenge tree descends topic → challenge → insight. Any concept may hold paper leaves in papers[]. Both tree types share this one structure.

summary.description: Optional prose intro for this concept, rendered under a '内容简介' subsection. Authored by the host LLM; lives in the JSON, so re-rendering the tree is idempotent (edit here, not in the markdown).

novelty_anchor.description: resource_id of the FIRST paper that proposed this concept — the node-level novelty anchor. By node kind: task=类1, pipeline=类2, module=类3; on a challenge tree an insight node may anchor the first paper to propose that idea (a challenge node usually has none — challenges are identified, not proposed). A verifiable priority fact, not a value judgment. 类4 (papers that merely improve an existing pipeline/module with a new module) are NOT anchors and get no schema field — they are ordinary members of the papers[] of the node they refine; see the build-literature-tree SKILL.

anchor_note.description: Optional free-text source/justification for the anchor (e.g. 'first stated in Sec. 3'). Not enforced or validated.

papers.description: resource_id refs of paper leaves classified under this concept.
